evidence: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5,12 - getElementById('discourse-comments') result is used unguarded in comments.appendChild(iframe); if the host page lacks the container a TypeError is thrown. It only happens when the embedding site misconfigures the snippet, so this is a low-severity robustness fix.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 - `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. Any origin that is a prefix/substring of discourseUrl passes (e.g. discourseUrl 'https://forum.example.com/' accepts origin 'https://forum.example.co'). The 'path/query' wording is slightly off, but the substring flaw is real. Impact is limited to resizing the iframe. Fix: compare e.origin against the parsed origin of discourseUrl exactly.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:20-21 - e.data.height is concatenated with 'px' and assigned to iframe.height without validation. A bad value only produces an invalid height attribute (no injection, since it is a property assignment), and the origin check gates it. Parsing with parseInt is cheap hardening.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 uses Kernel#open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) and app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 uses open(url). Kernel#open with open-uri accepts file paths and '|cmd' pipes, so URI.parse(url).open is safer. However, feed_polling_url is an admin-only site setting (config/site_settings.yml:353-357). The user-reachable path (embed_url) is constrained by TopicRetriever#invalid_host? (lib/topic_retriever.rb:14-19), which requires URI(url).host == embeddable_host, so internal hosts, metadata endpoints and file:// cannot be reached through it. The SSRF severity is overstated.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 - `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. SimpleRSS returns nil for tags that are missing from an item (e.g. RSS 2.0 items with only <description>), which raises NoMethodError. Because poll_feed also runs inline from TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41), this also breaks retrieval. Fall back to i.description or skip the item.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 - feed_key is defined but grep shows no callers anywhere in app/lib/spec. It is dead code (probably intended for If-Modified-Since caching). Remove it or wire it up.

app/models/post.rb:133 returns raw unmodified for cook_method raw_html, skipping post_analyzer.cook and its sanitizer. app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 sets raw_html for all imports, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 renders `raw post.cooked`. import_remote whitelists tags/attributes via Readability (topic_embed.rb:48-50), but the RSS path (poll_feed.rb:35) passes feed HTML through unfiltered, so <script> or on* handlers in the feed become stored XSS on the forum origin. The source is admin-trusted by design, so the risk depends on how much the feed is trusted, but sanitizing is warranted.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates url into `#{url}` without escaping, and post.rb:133 skips sanitizing for raw_html posts. The only guard is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (topic_embed.rb:11), and Ruby ^ is line-anchored. A single quote is legal in URIs, so a URL such as http://host/'onmouseover='... from a feed link or embed_url breaks out of the attribute. Use ERB::Util.html_escape / link_to.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 `contents << ...`. In practice nil is unlikely: poll_feed would already fail at i.content.scrub (poll_feed.rb:35), and Readability#content returns a String. The bigger issue is that << mutates the caller's string argument (and would fail on frozen strings). Prefer `contents = contents.to_s + ...`.

lib/post_revisor.rb:11-13 - revise! returns false only when should_revise? is false, i.e. @post.raw == new_raw (post_revisor.rb:26-28). In that case the post already holds the absolutized content, so updating content_sha1 at topic_embed.rb:38 keeps the embed in sync with what is stored rather than desyncing it. A failed save does not make revise! return false either.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 open(url).read passes no open_timeout or read_timeout. Net::HTTP applies a default read_timeout (60s), so a read cannot hang forever, but connect had no default timeout in Ruby of that era. It runs in a Sidekiq job (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17), so a hang ties up a worker rather than a web request. Adding explicit timeouts is reasonable hardening.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:45-52 fetches before the https? check in import (line 11) runs. From TopicRetriever, invalid_host? (lib/topic_retriever.rb:14) requires a URI with host == embeddable_host, which rules out pipes and file paths but still allows e.g. ftp://embeddable_host. lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 passes t[:link] from an operator-supplied file with no checks. Validating the scheme (and using URI.parse(url).open instead of Kernel#open) is cheap defense in depth.

app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 `<%- end if %>` is a bug, but not strictly a syntax error. The compiled Ruby becomes `end if <next buffer-append statement>`, because Ruby continues the if-modifier onto the next line. So it likely parses but wraps the block in a bogus condition and emits template text out of order. Controller specs do not render views, so tests would not catch it. Change it to `<%- end %>`.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 - topic_embeds is a brand-new table introduced by this PR, so no existing data can be dropped when the migration first runs. force: true is also an established convention in this repo (e.g. db/migrate/20130328162943_create_hot_topics.rb:3, 20130411205132_create_admin_logs.rb:3, 20130416004933_group_users.rb:3).

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 - Rails never re-runs an already-applied migration, so adding force: true only matters on a fresh database where the table does not exist yet. top_topics is a derived score table that is regenerated from topics. The same force: true convention appears in many repo migrations (hot_topics, admin_logs, etc.).

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-29 - setnx followed by expire is non-atomic. If the process dies between the two calls, the key never expires and non-staff retrieval of that URL is blocked permanently. The window is tiny, and the same pattern is used elsewhere in the codebase (app/models/topic_link_click.rb:37, app/models/view.rb:17, app/models/user.rb:300). `$redis.set(key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)` would close the gap.

config/site_settings.yml:357 - embed_by_username is a string setting that defaults to '', so it is never nil and ''.downcase is safe. lib/topic_retriever.rb:49-50 then finds no user and returns on user.blank?. poll_feed is already guarded by embed_by_username.present? (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:17).

lib/post_creator.rb:216 - the only caller that passes cook_method is app/models/topic_embed.rb:22, which uses Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]. The option is internal and cannot come from user input, and any unknown integer simply falls through to normal cooking in post.rb:133-136. Validation adds no real value.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 - on PostgreSQL before 11 (current when this was written), ADD COLUMN with a non-null DEFAULT rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, which can be slow on large forums. This is real, but the pattern is common in this codebase's migrations and the column must be non-null for the cook_method comparison.

spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:34 uses be_true. Gemfile_rails4.lock:293-298 pins rspec 2.14, where be_true is the standard, non-deprecated matcher (the deprecation arrived in 2.99/3.0). The repo uses be_true in 268 places, and switching to `be true` would change semantics (identity vs truthiness).

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:35-38 places `response.should be_success` and the X-Frame-Options assertion in an after hook. This works, but failures are reported against the hook instead of the example and can produce doubled or confusing errors. Moving the assertions into each example (or a shared helper) is clearer. It is a test-readability issue, not a correctness bug.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25-38 has no rescue around open/SimpleRSS.parse or the per-item loop. As a scheduled job with retry: false, Sidekiq logs the exception, so a failure is not silent. However, lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 calls it inline, so a feed error aborts retrieval before the fetch_http fallback (line 45), and one bad item stops the remaining items. Rescuing around the fetch and per item is worthwhile.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:161-162 - the raw: p[:cooked], cooked: p[:cooked] lines are pre-existing and not changed by this PR. PostCreator ignores a :cooked option (lib/post_creator.rb:206-213 only passes raw through) and cooks raw itself, and Discourse's markdown pipeline accepts HTML in raw. Disqus exports only provide HTML, so there is no other source text available.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:163 `created_at: Date.parse(p[:created_at])` drops the time of day. PostCreator does `Time.zone.parse(@opts[:created_at].to_s)` (lib/post_creator.rb:217), so imported replies get midnight timestamps. This is accurate, but the line is pre-existing and not part of this PR's diff (the PR removed the other Date.parse use), and it only affects a one-off import task.

app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 `` - Rails 4 `<%= %>` output is HTML-escaped (including ' as '), so there is no injection. The same raw pattern is used in app/views/email/_post.html.erb:5. image_tag would add an alt attribute but gives no meaningful safety gain.
